account: RL-Math's weight change (0.24% of weight norm) does its work through its top-8 singular input-output pairs per matrix (about 12% of its squared norm): added at 1.5x to the cued base they reach RL on hard328 (64.2% against RL plain 64.0%, base 50.2%; vote +0.1 points) and capture 0.88 of RL's per-sample gain where the base gets 0 of 4, as a graded shift in every sample, while random rank-8, Think-SFT-top-8, base-own-top-8 or re-paired edits of the same norm give about nothing.

The pairs do two separable jobs: late layers and direction 1 are a finish dial that cuts cap hits (20% to 11-14%) but leaves never-solved problems at a fresh base sample's 0.05 and lowers accuracy above 2x (late 3x and 4.5x: 48%, 32%), while directions 2-8 and layers 0-21 shift each next-step choice toward RL's, which cuts slips, lifts finished-wrong problems (23% to 33%) and never-solved ones (0 to 0.15 per sample), and makes the edit's wrong answers agree with RL's (+0.29 over the base).

On-policy RL writes such pairs whatever the reward (top-8 share: LM-judge General-RL 0.127, Math 0.135, Think-SFT 0.030), in the matrices deliberative text drives (pattern follows Think-SFT, rho 0.59, not IF-RL) and on input directions the base already uses (Think-SFT's change 4.8x chance there, Code-RL's 5.2x Think-SFT's, code text drives them at 87% of math), with the reward choosing only the output side, so Code-RL's pairs lift plain math about halfway (157/250 against Math's 217) as a per-sample opening switch (deliberative m21 answers 94% right, others 36%) and Math's pairs barely help code (+1.5 points against Code's +7.0).

Inference copies only the opening and the finishing, plus selection among the base's own samples: the three-token cue is the deliberative opening that the first 100 RL steps install (step-100 plain 417.5 against cued base 410.5 of 500, same cap-hit rate, same vote gain +7.2 against +7.6), T 1.0 removes the repetition loops of T 0.6 (loop share past 4,096 tokens 0.52-0.63 against 0.004), and a vote over 4 turns sometimes-right into right because wrong answers mostly scatter (pair agreement 0.22-0.26).

So the base reaches the part of RL's gain on problems where it already writes a right sample (81% of the MATH-500 sample gap; vote 446-450 against RL 463-474) and misses the slip-rate part (hard328 vote 195 against RL 224, with no right base sample on 26 of the 36 problems RL's vote wins), and self-review, truncation, tie rules and text edits add 0-1.4 points because none changes the per-step choice distribution.

Hence a new edit's effect is set by which true RL pairs it contains, not by its norm, module type or the base's accuracy: layers 0-21 or directions 2-8 put base-0-of-4 hard328 problems at 0.10-0.19 per sample (layers 0-10 alone with cap hits near the base's 20%), late-only or direction-1 edits cut cap hits to 11-14% but stay at 0.05 there, mismatched-pair, random, Think-SFT or base-own edits of equal norm stay within 3 points of the base, Code-RL pairs give about half of Math's lift on math, and every edit peaks near 1.5x and falls by 2x (MATH-500 456 to 448).
